subtopic: Array and Two-Pointer / Sliding Window Techniques
question_text: In a sliding window algorithm computing the minimum size subarray sum at least `target` with positive integers, what is the amortized time complexity of the right and left pointer movements?

options.text: O(N log N) due to binary window expansion
O(N) because each pointer visits each element at most once
O(N * target) proportional to value magnitude

answer_explanation: Although the inner `while` loop contracts the left pointer, both `left` and `right` pointers advance monotonically from 0 to N. Thus, each element is enqueued and dequeued at most once, yielding strictly O(N) amortized time.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: C. Rationale: Although the inner `while` loop contracts the left pointer, both `left` and `right` pointers advance monotonically from 0 to N. Thus, each element is enqueued and dequeued at most once, yielding strictly O(N) amortized time.
